models_evaluated: Internally developed AI algorithm for MR-derived total kidney volume segmentation in ADPKD

links.outcome: Difference between AI segmentation and radiologist/technologist-edited segmentation in TKV after clinician review
links.effect: Of 170 reviewed cases, 84 were manually edited; AI TKV output showed a small mean volume difference of -3.3% versus edited; disease class differed in five cases.
links.quote: Of manually edited cases (n=84), the AI-algorithm TKV output showed a small mean volume difference of -3.3%.

links.outcome: Whether validated AI performance was preserved when implemented in local clinical practice
links.effect: Algorithm showed high agreement and was noninferior to interobserver variability; performance preserved when implementation environment matched development conditions.
links.quote: Performance of an AI algorithm in real-life clinical practice can be preserved if there is careful development and validation and if the implementation environment closely matches the development conditions.

screen.reason: Evaluates the prospective real-world clinical deployment of an AI algorithm for measuring total kidney volume, specifically assessing quality control through clinician review and manual editing of outputs.

primary.practice: expert manual review and editing of AI segmentations
